Abdur Rashid Khan, Advocate with Md. Shahidul Haque Khan, Advocate ------ For the Petitioner.

Md. Salahuddin & another ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Abdul Hakim & another ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J: This Rule was issued U/S 439 and 561A Cr.P.C. calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and the Opposite Party No. 1 to show cause why the proceedings in Complaint Case No.1068A of 1977 pending in the Court of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (S), Dhaka should not be quashed. 

 2. The opposite party No.1 Abdul Hakim, Manager, Salam Industries filed a petition of complaint on 16-6-77 in the Court of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (South), Dhaka alleging inter alia that he is a bonafide business man and has been manufacturing agricultural implements of larger kind for Rice Hauler Machines, Rice Hauler Knives, Rice Hauler Shells and Rice Hauler Screens (being parts of Rice Hauler Machines under the Trade Mark Nawka brand) for the last 10 years and has got wide reputation in the market of Bangladesh. The Nawka brand was registered under Trade Mark Registration No. 48, 337 in Class 7 on 23-3-67 and a certificate was obtained from the Karachi Office and subsequently the complainant registered the Trade Mark in Bangladesh as per Summary Registration No.10036 and obtained certificate on 28-12-76. The complainant filed the petition against one Abdus Sattar Bhuiyan as proprietor of Agrani Prakaushali located at 538, Nayatola, Magh Bazar, P.S. Tejgaon, District Dhaka. He further alleged that the said accused person knowing full well the reputation of the Nawka brand Rice Hauler Screen made by the complainant began to produce the same Rice Hauler Screen under the name M/S. Agrani Prakaushali with its factory at 538, Nayatola, Magh Bazar, Dhaka. He has also been marketing the said products at shops called Habibia Traders, 217, Nawabpur, Dhaka, Rajdhani Machinery, 95, Nawabpur, Dhaka and Micho Machinery, 98, Nawabpur, Dhaka. The complainant alleged that the accused person has thus committed an offence U/S 481 of the Penal Code by using a false property mark and he is liable to be punished U/S 482 of the Penal Code for using a false Trade Mark or property mark. 

 3. The petitioners Md. Salah Uddin and Abdur Rashid Bhuiyan state in their application that the firm M/S. Agrani Prakaushali Karkhana located at 538, Nayatola, Magh Bazar, P.S. Tejgaon District Dhaka is not a proprietary firm and the said accused person Abdus Sattar Bhuiyan is not a proprietor thereof M/S. Agrani Prakaushali Karkhana located at 538, Nayatola, Magh Bazar, P.S. Tejgaon, District Dhaka is a partnership firm of which the petitioners are the only partners. The complainant opposite party knowing full well the names of the partners of the said firm deliberately 'mentioned the name of one Abdus Sattar Bhuiyan as a proprietor of the said firm with a malafide intention. 

 5. The petitioners further alleged in their application that before filing the present petition of complaint, the complainant opposite party instituted Title Suit No. 8/77 on 5-5-77 in the Court of the District Judge, Dhaka for permanent injunction and for damages for infringement of registered Trade Mark Nawka brand against the firm M/S. Agrani Prakaushali Karkhana on the same allegations as made in the petition of complaint. On 21-5-77 the complainant opposite party obtained an exparte order of temporary injunction against the said firm. As against the said exparte order, the said firm preferred F.M.A. No. 220/77 and also obtained an ad-interim stay of operation of the order of temporary injunction from this Court. 

 8. It is also found that prior to the filing of the petition of complaint the complainant opposite party filed Title Suit No. 8/77 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Dhaka for permanent injunction and for damages for infringement of registered trade mark Nawka brand on the same allegations as made in the petition of complaint and that the suit is still pending. In the case of Ruppell V. Ponnusami Tevan, (1899) I.L.R. 22 Mad. 488 it was held, "Ordinarily the infringement of a trade mark is rather a civil than a criminal wrong, but as civil proceedings may require much time and expenditure to bring them to a conclusion, the Legislature, in its anxiety to protect traders, has allowed of resort to the criminal Courts to provide a speedy remedy in cases where the aggrieved party is diligent and does not by his conduct show that the case is not one of urgency. If, therefore, the person aggrieved fails to resort to the criminal Courts within a year of the offence coming to his knowledge, the law assumes that the case is not one of urgency, and it leaves him to his civil remedy by an action for injunction." 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The proceedings contained in complaint Case No. 1068A of 1977 pending in the Court of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (South), Dhaka are quashed.
